target_customer: Online grocers, delivery apps and retailers that want to accept SNAP EBT payments
problem: Over 42 million Americans receive SNAP benefits but most merchants could not accept EBT online. Forage provides one API, checkout components and a fraud layer to do it.
business_model: B2B payments API with transaction based fees

founders.name: Ofek Lavian
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in the PayPal Ventures release of 2022-08. Aggregators give conflicting education and an Instacart payments role; not confirmed from an opened source.

founders.name: Victor E. Fimbres
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

competitors.name: Instacart (Carrot Payments)
competitors.what: Built its own online SNAP EBT acceptance after the USDA online pilot began in 2019
competitors.traction_then: About 80 to 90 of the under 100 retailers accepting online SNAP in 2021 went through Instacart

competitors.name: Fiserv and FIS Worldpay
competitors.what: Incumbent payment processors that became USDA approved online SNAP EBT processors alongside Forage

technical_complexity.rationale: A PCI compliant API over government EBT networks, PIN handling and USDA certification is standard fintech engineering with heavy compliance.

defensibility.rationale: USDA approval is held by only a few processors, which is a structural barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large retailers and Instacart built in house; Forage won the long tail of grocers and became one of three approved providers by 2022-08.

market_need_then: Over 42 million SNAP recipients per the company, with online grocery growing and USDA's online purchasing pilot opening in 2019.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven: Payments powering people; Built by developers, for developers

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; the name is generic and shared with other Forage companies, though the mission message is clear.

outcome_analysis: Forage is active and growing: it raised a $22M Series A in 2022-08 and a $40M Series B in 2026-06, and lists itself as one of three USDA approved online EBT providers. Its moat is regulatory approval in a niche large incumbents were slow to serve, plus rising online grocery demand.
notes: Series B from several outlets in search results (Pulse 2.0, Fintech Global, VCA Online), not opened individually. Caplight lists a Series A extension dated 2023-11 with no amount, unverified. Total raised figures of $62.1M and $75M conflict. A Glassdoor review mentions an acquisition around 2024, likely a different company named Forage and contradicted by the 2026 Series B, so ignored. Competitor sources are dated 2022-08 but describe the 2019 to 2021 situation.
